description:
Tailscode is the native Mac window for every coding agent running on your own machines. Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, opencode and Oh My Pi, plus any agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol, on any model they can run, including one on your own graphics card: start them, watch six at once, steer them and read what they did, while each repository stays on the machine that owns it. Your chats go point to point over your own Tailscale network, never through a relay, with no sign-in. Free and open source.

ONE COMMAND TO SET UP
For Claude Code, one line on the computer you code on installs the bridge and ends with a pairing link. Paste it, confirm, and Tailscode has your machine; opencode has a one-line installer too. Want to look first? A built-in demo shows the main screens with no server at all.

HERMES AND ANY ACP AGENT
• Hermes, Gemini CLI, Codex, goose and the rest of the ACP registry run through the bridge already on your machine, each proved with a real chat before it counts as ready.
• Hermes with no model gets one in a tap from the model server your machine already runs. It sits in the model pill beside Claude.
• Press ⌥⏎ to ask later, or type when: weekdays 7:30. Your machine asks with your Mac asleep, remembers the last run and stays quiet when nothing changed.

EVERY AGENT AT A GLANCE
• The Agents window shows what needs you, what is working and what finished in the last hour, with approve, answer, nudge and stop, a peek inspector, and a wall of every agent to leave on a spare screen.
• The sidebar puts who needs you first, then what is working, pinned, saved and recent.
• Split the window into panes and put a different machine, project or conversation in each.

ANY MODEL, EVEN YOUR OWN GPU
• Whatever your agent can run, from cloud models to a local model served by Ollama or llama.cpp on your own machine, picked per chat with its reasoning effort.
• Carry a conversation to another model with a short brief, or keep a party of six one chord away.

A LIVE, NATIVE TRANSCRIPT
• Megatron folds a turn's thinking and tool runs into one head you open to read, search and replay every step.
• Syntax-highlighted code with copy, and a diff for every Edit or Write the agent makes.
• Approvals, questions as answerable cards, subagents in place; queue a follow-up or stop the turn on the server.
• The repository, read-only on purpose: branch, drift, changed files and their diffs.

ASK FROM ANYWHERE
• One global hotkey opens the ask box over any app and sends the question to the machine you choose.
• Not only code: ask what is eating the GPU, research a question, tidy a folder.
• Notifications when a turn needs you or finishes.

WHERE THE MONEY WENT
• Every conversation priced turn by turn, every month totalled across machines, by model, project and tool. Always an estimate, never a bill.
• Plan limits and quotas per provider and account, with the pace and turns left.

YOURS, END TO END
• Your chats travel point to point over your tailnet, never through a relay. No sign-in, no ads, no tracking, and your code and conversations never reach us.
• Native AppKit, Swift 6, Liquid Glass, real menus, VoiceOver labels.
• Open source under GPL-3.0: the app, the engine and the bridges. Also on iPhone, iPad and Linux.

FREE, WITH AN HONEST PRO
Every screen but the delegate board is in the free app, on one server, for good. Tailscode Pro is a one-time purchase, no subscription: unlimited servers in one list, iPhone and Mac on the same Apple Account, and the delegate board.

REQUIREMENTS
A computer on your Tailscale network (free for personal use) running opencode, Claude Code or Hermes and any ACP agent through claude-bridge, or Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. Tailscode is independent open-source software, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, Nous Research, Tailscale Inc., the opencode project or Oh My Pi.

Privacy policy: https://midgarcorp.cc/tailscode/privacy
Source code: https://github.com/guitaripod/Tailscode
promotionalText: Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Hermes in a native Mac app: every agent on your own machines, live, on any model, even your own GPU. No sign-in.
whatsNew:
Masters, a terminal on your own machine, and a Quick Ask that is always ready.

New:
• Masters (beta): give a Claude Code machine a standing role with a charter, skills, a notebook and checks the machine proves. Each task is a fresh chat briefed with all of it and ends in a debrief whose notebook changes you accept or skip. Masters sit among the sidebar's places. With claude-bridge 1.38.
• A terminal pane: your login shell on the machine the chat works on. The shell stays there, so it is waiting after you quit or move to another device, and a split opens in the folder it stands in. With claude-bridge 1.38 or omp-bridge 0.19.
• Quick Ask is always ready: Tailscode can start at login and live in the menu bar, so the shortcut answers with no window open, and your keyboard goes back to the app you asked over.
• Outer Rim, a theme that is a place: a starfield behind the chat and every signal a coloured blade. New installs start in it.
• Your phone stays quiet while you are at this Mac: it holds its notices and Live Activities until you leave, and a notice goes away once its chat is read anywhere. With claude-bridge 1.34 or omp-bridge 0.18.
• Pictures open from where they sit, gather in one strip under their turn, and only the ones the agent names are shown. A long prompt folds.
• A message written offline waits and goes on its own when the machine answers, even after a relaunch, and the answer above a new question no longer replays as it is sent.
• Unread chats are easy to spot, each row says what happened, and the list of missed notices no longer repeats what the rows already say.
• Each tile on the Agents wall wears an emblem for its model, and tiles stay readable in a small window.
• First run asks which agent runs on your computer and opens on its install command.

Fixes:
• Quick Ask's words and caret sit level with its placeholder, and its buttons sit on the first line.
• The Pro window opens at the size of its page instead of as a bare title bar.
• A usage window whose reset time has passed no longer reads as used up.
• A background command finishing is a quiet note, not a message in your voice.
• Old chats no longer light up as unread.
